AYwlilwYA/ColorOS16-LiquidGlass.description: An LSPosed module that implements iOS 26-style Liquid Glass effects for the notification center / control center of ColorOS 16
AYwlilwYA/ColorOS16-LiquidGlass.body:
# ColorOS16 Liquid Glass

An LSPosed module that implements **iOS 26-style Liquid Glass** animation effects for the notification center / control center of **ColorOS 16**.

It does not modify system APKs or replace the View structure. By hooking ColorOS's built-in blur pipeline, it intercepts the unblurred original image and uses a custom AGSL shader to fully render the liquid glass effect (blur + SDF rounded-corner refraction + dispersion + highlights).

> **Current status**: In development / experimental. All features are disabled by default; behavior before enabling is identical to when the module is not installed.

---

## Effect

Applies a liquid glass material to the blur-based controls in the notification center / control center (notification cards, quick toggles, media cards, slider capsules, etc.): a clear inner lens, edge refraction bands, spectral dispersion, directional highlights, and vibrancy boost.

## How It Works

```
ColorOS blur pipeline (com.oplus.posteffect)
        │
        ├─ hook intercepts the unblurred original image (HardwareBuffer)
        │
        ↓
   Custom AGSL RuntimeShader
   (SDF rounded rectangle + refraction displacement + dispersion + highlights + vibrancy)
        │
        ↓
   Replaces the system's pure blur + blend draw output
```

Key points:

- **Only modifies rendering, not structure**: does not replace Views, add overlays, or intrude into system internals, for maximum compatibility.
- **Background source maintenance**: full-screen snapshot + per-element region coordinate remapping. Sampling coordinates are remapped in real time as elements move, and no screen capture happens while static.
- **AGSL shader**: built on Android `RuntimeShader`. The algorithm is derived from [Kyant0/AndroidLiquidGlass](https://github.com/Kyant0/AndroidLiquidGlass) (Apache-2.0, see [THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md](https://github.com/AYwlilwYA/ColorOS16-LiquidGlass/blob/HEAD/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md)).

## Features

The module includes a built-in settings UI. Each item can be toggled independently, **all disabled by default**:

| Category | Contents |
|------|------|
| Liquid glass | Refraction strength, blur radius, vibrancy, highlight intensity / falloff, corner radius, etc. |
| Mask and text | Background darkening mask, text readability coloring (unified injection channel to avoid color jumps) |
| Desktop animations | Spring stiffness and damping for app open / close / interrupt animations, icon opacity duration |
| Tilt and perspective | 3D tilt effect for app switching (experimental) |
| Background and capture | Capture rate, downsampling factor, etc. |
| Other |…

DerpZhenjun/LabourLawyer.body:
# LabourLawyer

**Choose a region, fill in information, generate labour arbitration documents.**

A document and procedure assistant for ordinary workers. Fill in the arbitration application, organize the evidence list, then check local official material requirements and submission methods. No need to create a case or learn a management system first.

> This platform is a labour arbitration assistance tool, **not an official government service website**. Documents are not guaranteed to be accepted; jurisdiction, materials, and acceptance conditions are subject to the latest judgment of the local arbitration institution.

## Software download (preview)

[Download Android and Windows clients: v1.1.0-preview.2](https://github.com/DerpZhenjun/LabourLawyer/releases/tag/v1.1.0-preview.2)

The Android APK is a USB debugging package; Windows offers an installer and a portable version. The installation package includes the client interface of this preview version. The latest district/county forms follow the current web source code. **The backend and official template library must still be started as described in this document. AI connects to Ubuntu Qwen3.8; models do not run on Windows.** They cannot generate documents offline on their own, and they do not indicate that nationwide district/county integration is complete. After downloading, you can verify files with `SHA256SUMS.txt` on the same page. For detailed steps and the actual test scope, see the [release notes](https://github.com/DerpZhenjun/LabourLawyer/blob/HEAD/docs/releases/v1.1.0-preview.2.md).

## From filling to submission

1. Select province, city, district/county, or functional zone. The handling area must be confirmed based on place of work, employer location, etc.; do not select based only on household registration.
2. Choose an application or evidence list. The form provides clearly labeled fictional examples; replace them with your own information before formal use.
3. Start with one piece of evidence and add more as needed. You may confirm or cancel before generation; after confirmation, download the Word document.
4. Review local page counts, window addresses, and handling methods. Verified official entries provide links; login or captcha is completed by the user on the official website.

Supports generating reference documents when information is incomplete; required materials must still be completed before submission. Official blank templates, official samples, and platform-assisted documents are labeled separately, and samples are not passed off as blank forms.

## Every region uses its own sources

The system matches matters, handling authorities, materials, and attachments by specific region, and retains official links, collection time, verification status, and file SHA-256 values. Switching regions re-queries; where there is no local source, it shows pending verification and does not inherit data from neighboring regions.

**Public release data updated 2026-10-29. Nationwide district/county coverage is not yet complete.**

Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
```

Nu0vo1212/Rust-Frp.description: Rust-based Frp client/server, compatible with the original Go version of Frp
Nu0vo1212/Rust-Frp.body:
---

NFrp is a Rust reimplementation of [fatedier/frp](https://github.com/fatedier/frp), **fully compatible with the official wire protocol v1 and v2**, and can interoperate directly with the official `frps` / `frpc` (tested against v0.71.0). Configurations issued by third-party frp platforms also work directly.

By default it uses **v1**, matching the default of official frp, so official clients / servers **do not need any configuration changes** to connect.

Resource usage is very small: the server's resident memory is about 3.5 MB (under the same load, the Go version frps uses 28.8~31.8 MB), single-file deployment, no runtime dependencies.

> **Full documentation**: <https://nu0vo1212.github.io/Rust-Frp/>
> Covers installation, all configuration options, the eight proxy types, detailed wire protocol (v1 / v2), ACL / RBAC, audit logs, HTTP API, and security fix history.
> Source files are in [`docs/`](https://github.com/Nu0vo1212/Rust-Frp/blob/HEAD/docs/); local preview: `python -m http.server -d docs 8899`

## Installation

### Option 1: crates.io (recommended for Rust users)

All three crates are published, and you can also depend directly on the protocol library **without running the tunneling service**:

```bash
# Install the two executables
cargo install nfrp-server nfrp-client
```

```toml
# Or: use only the protocol / config / encryption as a library
[dependencies]
nfrp-common = "0.6"
```

| crate | Purpose | Link |
|---|---|---|
| **nfrp-common** | Protocol, config, encryption, ACL/RBAC, logging, transport abstraction | [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/nfrp-common) · [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/nfrp-common) |
| **nfrp-server** | Server executable (equivalent to official `frps`) | [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/nfrp-server) |
| **nfrp-client** | Client executable (equivalent to official `frpc`) | [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/nfrp-client) |

> **About version numbers**: versions on crates.io and the versions on this page's Releases are **independent of each other**.

SAOS-3624/dsh-video-storyboard.description: Scene-aware storyboard for DeepSeek Harness: 9-16 numbered cells with timestamps + transcript + an audio envelope, packed into ONE image (384 tokens). Two tools: video_storyboard and video_zoom.
SAOS-3624/dsh-video-storyboard.body:
# dsh-video-storyboard

> Let AI truly "watch" a video: **one storyboard image + a text list with timecodes**, so the model can answer "what happens at minute 3" and "which cell does this line correspond to".
>
> English: [README.en.md](https://github.com/SAOS-3624/dsh-video-storyboard/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)
>
> Listed in [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin).

---

## What problem it solves

Multimodal models have two clumsy ways of watching video:

- **Frame-by-frame extraction** — extracting at 1 fps from a 10-minute video yields 600 images, and the tokens explode.
- **Subtitles only** — all visual information (composition, actions, scene changes) is lost.

This plugin takes a third route: **compress the visuals into one grid image** (capped at 384 tokens), accompanied by a **time-aligned text list** (start and end time of each cell + the dialogue within that cell + how many cuts it contains).

The model gets "what happened in these 90 seconds and roughly at which second". When it needs detail, it uses `video_zoom` to enlarge a specific segment.

## Four tools

| Tool | What it does | When to use it |
|---|---|---|
| `video_probe` | Read-only container header: duration, resolution, frame rate, whether there are audio/subtitle tracks, whether it has already been analyzed | **Call it first when you first encounter a video**; it uses no image tokens |
| `video_storyboard` | Produces the grid image + text list | Main feature |
| `video_zoom` | Look at only one segment (a smaller time window, denser cells) | After reviewing the list and finding a segment important, zoom in |
| `video_locate` | **Pure text**: one sentence → timecode | You know what was said but not the minute it occurs |

## Installation

**The complete step-by-step guide (including dependencies, self-check, and troubleshooting) is in [docs/INSTALL.zh.md](https://github.com/SAOS-3624/dsh-video-storyboard/blob/HEAD/docs/INSTALL.zh.md).**

The three-line version:

```bash
winget install Gyan.FFmpeg          # required: ffmpeg + ffprobe
pip install --user -U yt-dlp        # only needed if you paste Bilibili/YouTube links
node scripts/install-dev.mjs        # install the plugin, then restart DSH
```

Starfie1d1272/Mizar.body:
**[Download the Windows installer (NJU cloud drive)](https://box.nju.edu.cn/d/91dec4c27e5d47f38fcf/?p=/Downloads)** · [Full GitHub downloads and release notes](https://github.com/Starfie1d1272/Mizar/releases)

For first-time use, choose the lightweight Windows x64 installer whose name ends with `-WebInstaller.exe` and follow the wizard to complete installation. The portable ZIP is for extracting and running, with you managing the program directory yourself. Historical versions and checksum files are available on GitHub Releases. For installation and upgrade steps, see [Quick Start](https://github.com/Starfie1d1272/Mizar/blob/HEAD/docs/guide/quick-start.md).

Mizar is an open-source production system built for campus and community CS2 tournaments. From pre-match introductions to post-match freeze frames, it gives matches a coherent program flow, a unified visual package, and on-site tools that commentators and directors can use at hand.

_Match footage, the large radar, and production controls are all within sight. [See more screenshots](https://github.com/Starfie1d1272/Mizar/blob/HEAD/docs/screenshots/README.md)._

## The program follows the match as it unfolds

Pre-match waiting, BP display, matchup opening, in-game HUD, halftime stats, and post-match results: Mizar reads game progress via GSI and, combined with tournament data, automatically advances the program and switches OBS scenes. Fewer repetitive actions, more energy left for the match.

When live adjustments are needed, you can take manual control at any time. You decide when to resume automation.

_Map bans, picks, and the decider map are shown in sequence, so viewers can follow both teams' map plans. [View static screenshot](https://github.com/Starfie1d1272/Mizar/blob/HEAD/docs/screenshots/program-veto.png)._

## See the match, and control the broadcast

In the Windows production workstation, view live CS2 footage, the large radar, and match data all at once. Commentators can more easily grasp the overall picture, and directors can confirm the on-site situation through periodic OBS preview frames, stream status, and Bilibili live status.

# WWA Wing
This is a TypeScript / JavaScript implementation of the internet RPG "[World Wide Adventure](http://wwajp.com/)".

2. Following the installation instructions at [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/ja/installation), install pnpm.
  - The pnpm version actually used is determined by the `packageManager` field in [`package.json`](https://github.com/WWAWing/WWAWing/blob/HEAD/package.json). Because there is a mechanism that automatically determines the pnpm version actually used, any version of pnpm v10 or later is fine (using the newest version is recommended).

mw2wbyys6t-sudo/live2d-auto-pipeline.body:
From text description → AI character art → automatic layering → Live2D model → exportable and previewable.

---

## First, let’s be clear: what it can do now

I don’t want to make empty promises. Some parts of this project are already solid, and some are still in progress. Below is the **actual status as of v0.10.9**:

| Capability | Status | Notes |
|------|------|------|
| AI-generated character art | ✅ Available | Pollinations free cloud, works out of the box with no key; also supports paid high-quality generation via Volcano Engine/SenseTime |
| Fully offline image generation | ✅ Available | Automatically falls back to placeholder art when offline, so the pipeline doesn’t stop |
| Automatic layering (K-means) | ✅ Available | Color-clustering-based layering, pure Python, no extra models needed |
| Automatic layering (SAM semantic) | ⚠️ Requires setup | Higher-precision semantic segmentation, but requires downloading about 2 GB of model weights |
| PSD export | ✅ Available | Requires `pip install psd-tools`; if missing, it falls back to exporting a PNG package |
| Live2D moc3 export | ✅ Available | **In-house compiler, pixel-by-pixel verified against Live2D’s official Cubism Core** |
| Face-tracking driver | ✅ Bundled in installer | The desktop build uses native Rust face tracking (YuNet + `onnxruntime.dll`); **no Python or MediaPipe install needed**; MediaPipe is used only when running from source. CI has verified that the exe, models, and dll are all present; the driver’s effect has not been tested with a live camera |
| Desktop pet mode | ⚠️ Not verified on hardware | pygame is bundled, but multi-window and always-on-top behavior has not been verified on real hardware |
| LLM chat + voice | ⚠️ Requires key | Chat requires an OpenAI/Anthropic API key or a local Ollama |
| Offline dependencies | ✅ Bundled in installer | Embedded CPython 3.12 + offline packages (site-packages about 0.9 GB); runs right after installation with no separate Python install. The torch group (used by SAM2) is downloaded on demand |

> In short: **the core “generate → layer → export” pipeline is fully usable, and the installer includes the runtime**; advanced interaction (LLM chat) requires your own key, and face tracking / desktop pet still await on-hardware verification.

---

## What problem this project solves

I’m a tech enthusiast myself, not a professional illustrator or modeler. I wanted to create my own virtual avatar, but I found that:

- Hiring an illustrator for one character art: **several hundred to several thousand yuan**
- Hiring someone to do Live2D rigging: **several thousand to tens of thousands of yuan**
- Learning it yourself: **PS layering, Live2D Cubism, and parameter tuning each take several months**

nh59yytyd5-dev/chinalaw-cli.description: China law and regulation search CLI for AI agents
nh59yytyd5-dev/chinalaw-cli.body:
`chinalaw` organizes publicly available laws, administrative regulations, and judicial interpretations into a database that can be queried article by article. Every returned article comes with its validity status, effective date, version, official source, and verification time: a model can propose leads, but citations must go back to the original text retrieved by the tool, so both humans and agents can review them. It does not answer legal questions and does not replace legal judgment.

```console
$ chinalaw article 民法典 533 --format md
## Civil Code, Article 533

> After a contract is formed, if its basis changes materially due to circumstances the parties could not have foreseen when concluding it, which do not constitute commercial risk, and continued performance would be manifestly unfair to one party, the adversely affected party may renegotiate with the other party. If no agreement is reached within a reasonable period, either party may request that the people's court or arbitration institution modify or terminate the contract.
The people's court or arbitration institution shall modify or terminate the contract based on the actual circumstances of the case and the principle of fairness.

---
- Text status: current
- Effective date: 2021-01-01
- Current version: published 2020-05-28 / effective 2021-01-01
- Source: https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf
- Last verified: verified 181 days ago
```

The same dataset can be used in four ways, which can be combined:

| Use | Suited for | Where the data is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Public law snapshot](https://law.newcombmath.com/about/data.html) | Research, batch processing, offline use | JSON / SQLite downloaded to your own machine |
| CLI and local MCP | Agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor; personal research | Local SQLite; contracts and case materials never leave the machine |
| [Hosted MCP](https://law.newcombmath.com/about/mcp.html) | Light online queries, trial use | law.newcombmath.com; read-only tokens available on request |
| Self-hosted service | Teams, multiple clients | Your own server: browser admin panel and read-only REST / MCP HTTP |

## A verifiable citation

1. **Locate**: if you know the law and article number, retrieve the original text directly (`article`). If the law's name is uncertain, first resolve its full name and candidates (`resolve`, which supports colloquial names, short names, and document numbers).
2. **Verify**: the same article number may correspond to different versions. Check whether the text matches your question, along with its validity status, effective date, and source. For past events, check the version that was in force at the time (`--as-of`). For time-validity leads, see `applicable` (it provides leads only, not conclusions).

slovx2/litch.body:
# Litch

**Simplified Chinese** | [English](https://github.com/slovx2/litch/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

Litch aims to deliver a comfortable desktop client and remote connection experience.

- Direct SSH connection
- Mobile (Android) direct SSH to remote devices; works even when the desktop app is not running
- Built-in browser and Computer Use (macOS, Windows)
- When a desktop is connected, remote devices can use the desktop browser and Computer Use, and after your approval can also run commands and read/write files on this computer
- Session tree (spawn sub-sessions across harnesses, report back, and wake up) and scheduled tasks (run on the device on time, even when the desktop app is closed)
- Scan a QR code to bind a remote device already configured on the desktop to your phone, without setting up SSH keys on the phone

## Interface

### Geek retro (default)

### Literary humanities

Screenshots show demo data. Theme, light/dark mode, and language (Chinese / English) can be switched at any time.

## Features

- **Remote connection.** Connects through your own ssh config and keys, with no ports opened on either side; reconnects automatically after disconnects without losing turns.
- **Multiple harnesses.** Claude Code, Pi, Codex, plus the experimental DeepSeek Harness (DSH), OpenCode, and ACP agents (Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, etc.), all in one window.
- **Built-in browser.** Shared by you and the agent; the remote localhost is automatically forwarded over ssh.
- **Computer Use (macOS, Windows).** The agent operates any app on this computer without per-app approval; a notice appears on screen during operation, and pressing Esc stops it.
- **Operate this computer.** Agents on remote devices can, after your approval, run commands, read/write files, and copy files between the two machines on the desktop computer; off by default, enabled per device.
- **Session tree.** Sessions can spawn sub-sessions, across harnesses: a Claude Code session can spawn Codex, Pi, etc. sub-sessions, and vice versa. Sub-sessions sit under their parent; on completion they report back to the parent and, if needed, wake it up to keep working.
- **Scheduled tasks.** Tasks are stored on the device and run on schedule by the device; they keep running when the desktop is closed or disconnected. Each run either starts a new session or continues in an existing one.
- **Pair phone by QR code.** The desktop app (or `litch pair` on that machine) shows a QR code. Scanning it with your phone generates the phone's own key and registers it on that machine; you check the confirmation code on your computer and click allow. The computer's key never leaves the computer, and each phone can be revoked individually.

takara9/marmot.description: A simple, fast virtual server execution environment for verification, experimentation, and learning
takara9/marmot.body:
# Marmot — A simple, Kubernetes-ready private cloud you can start with a single server

**Just write YAML and run `mactl create -f`**, and within minutes you get "virtual servers", "virtual networks", "storage", and even "Kubernetes clusters" and "NLB/ALB" on a single Linux server in your hands.

*English: Marmot is a simple, declarative private cloud built on KVM. Define VMs, networks, volumes and even Kubernetes clusters in YAML, and run them from a single Ubuntu server.*

---

## Marmot in 30 seconds

Create virtual machines the same way you would write a Kubernetes manifest.

```yaml
# server-20.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Server
metadata:
    name: server-20
spec:
    cpu: 1
    memory: 1024
    mmImage: ubuntu24.04
    auth:
        publicKey: "ssh-ed25519 AAAA... For marmot VMs"   # your own public key
        users:
         - ubuntu
    networkInterface:
        - networkname: host-bridge
```

```console
$ mactl create -f server-20.yaml
$ mactl get server
NAME        NODE      STATUS    CPU  RAM(MB)  IP-ADDRESS     NETWORK       AGE
----        ----      ------    ---  -------  ----------     -------       ---
server-20   marmot3   RUNNING   1    1024     192.168.1.20   host-bridge   5s

$ mactl ssh -i vmkey ubuntu@server-20       # SSH by server name, with no DNS configuration
ubuntu@server-20:~$
```

# 连板档案 · Local Shared Edition

Sharing the local test edition with others: the current shared edition **2026.10.28** has pages and business programs synced from the test edition **dfde734**, including tag hierarchy management, main-board time-sharing, node timeline, and note history. No Codex, account, Token, or Node.js is required, and Python does not need to be installed in advance.

## Simple Installation Guide

Supports **Windows 10/11 x64**. The computer must be able to reach GitHub. Python and Git do not need to be preinstalled, and no GitHub account is needed. Either of the two methods below is enough.

### Method 1: Hand It to an AI Agent

Send the following text to an AI Agent that can operate your computer:

```text
Please install and start the “连板档案” shared edition on this machine. GitHub author: x107108, project name: lianban-archive-desktop.
First install the latest stable release following the project's AI installation instructions, keeping the original features, interface, and existing personal data. After verifying it works, tell me the access address and how to start and stop it. If you cannot operate this machine, state that honestly.
```

This instruction contains no URL. The Agent can locate this repository using the author and project name, then complete installation and verification following the [AI installation instructions](https://github.com/x107108/lianban-archive-desktop/blob/HEAD/AI_INSTALL.md).

### Method 2: One-Line PowerShell Installation

Search for and open **PowerShell** from the Start menu, copy the entire command below, paste it, and press Enter:

```powershell
irm 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/x107108/lianban-archive-desktop/main/install-online.ps1' | iex
```

Wait for the program to automatically complete **download, verification, extraction, installation, and startup**. Once the browser opens the website, you can start using it.

### How to Use After Installation

Note the install directory and website address shown when installation finishes.

- **Start the website:** double-click `start_demo.cmd` in the install directory.
- **Stop the website:** double-click `stop_demo.cmd`.
- **Check for updates:** click “站内信” (in-site messages) at the top right of the website.

Personal tags, blacklist, and notes are saved on your own computer.
